name: lcs
why: A satirical ncurses political strategy game is a strange old-school curio, though deprecated and low-install, so only borderline.

brief.what_it_is: Liberal Crime Squad is a satirical, console-based political role-playing and strategy game. The player recruits a team of Elite Liberal radicals and tries to save the United States from a descent into Arch-Conservatism. The SourceForge page describes it as console/terminal software written in C++, and the brew metadata names the executable crimesquad. The page gives no detail on the exact input and output mechanics beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The page frames it as a satirical political game, and says its gameplay is based loosely on the classic 1983 RPG Oubliette.
brief.install_notes: The SourceForge page lists Linux and Windows as operating systems and gives no install steps, dependencies, or first-run instructions. I did not see a README or docs page with build or install details, so the brew formula is the only install path I can vouch for.
brief.standout: It is a satirical political recruit-a-squad RPG in the Oubliette lineage, which is an unusual niche. One reviewer says the developers' humor and thoroughness are NetHack-like, and that the source is manageable enough to contribute to.
brief.status: Quiet. The SourceForge page shows Last Update 2015-09-25, a project registration date of 2007-06-15, and 3 downloads this week. It has 7 reviews averaging 5.0 stars, with maintainers listed as grundee and jonathansfox. The page does not say the project is deprecated, so the scout note's 'deprecated' claim is not supported by anything I read.
brief.caveats: I read only the SourceForge project page, which had no README text and no docs. The scout note's 'ncurses' claim is not confirmed by this page, and 'low-install' is not supported either. The page's last update is about ten years old. It is GPLv2 licensed. The project's official website is linked on the page, but its URL was not shown in the text I received.
quotes: A satirical console-based political role-playing/strategy game in which you recruit a team of Elite Liberal radicals and try to save the United States from a descent into Arch-Conservatism.
Gameplay based loosely on the classic 1983 RPG Oubliette.

I love this game in many ways. It is extremely entertaining, features interesting political simulation and is carefully decorated by satire, irony and in some places almost NetHack-esque DevTeamThinksOfEverything.

judge.reason: Its satirical political premise paired with squad-based role-playing and political simulation is a genuinely unusual game concept, not merely a terminal novelty.

entry.title: Liberal Crime Squad
entry.tldr: A satirical terminal strategy RPG where you recruit Elite Liberal radicals to stop the United States sliding into Arch-Conservatism.
entry.deeper_look:
Liberal Crime Squad is a console-based political role-playing and strategy game written in C++. You recruit a team of radicals and try to steer the country away from what the project calls a descent into Arch-Conservatism. The tone is satire throughout.

Its gameplay is, in the project's words, "based loosely on the classic 1983 RPG Oubliette." That puts it in a small lineage of text-mode games that turn a squad, a map of choices and a lot of consequences into a long campaign, with politics as the setting instead of dungeons.

One reviewer on the project page compares the developers' humor and thoroughness to NetHack, calling it "almost NetHack-esque DevTeamThinksOfEverything." The same reviewer says the source is manageable enough to contribute to, which makes it a possible door into reading an old C++ game codebase.

The project is old. The SourceForge page shows registration in 2007 and a last update in September 2015. The brief does not describe the controls or interface, so expect to learn them by playing.

try_this.what_happens: Launches the game in your terminal so you can start recruiting your squad.

entry.whats_unique: It is a political satire built on the Oubliette lineage of squad RPGs, which is an unusual niche. A reviewer compares its thoroughness to NetHack.
entry.caveats: The last SourceForge update was in 2015, the Homebrew formula is marked deprecated, and the brief found no README or documentation, so expect to figure out the controls yourself.
